- Overestimate early in the forecast horizon when sentiment is positive (especially >0.5) — model tends to overreact to bullish sentiment.
- Underestimate when sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.3) — model fails to capture downside risk or panic.
- Overshoot after sharp price spikes — model often peaks too early and then underperforms in the following days.
- Exhibit mean reversion bias — model frequently forecasts a “correct” mean after a spike, but fails to account for momentum or volatility clustering.
- Lag in response to sentiment shifts — model reacts slowly to sentiment turning points, especially when sentiment drops sharply.
- Overweight recent history in short-term forecasts — model overfits to recent price movements, ignoring sentiment-driven structural shifts.
- Underweight sentiment in long-term forecasts — model ignores sentiment when forecasting 30-day horizons, leading to underestimation of upward momentum or overestimation of downward drift.
